about: Drafts from Rebound's November 2026 pilot that were judged to repeat a DOE library question, each with the library question(s) it matched. 'same': the same answer from the same cue (or the same computation with the same numbers). 'template': the same method or fact with new numbers or a reversed cue. writer-replaced and writer-rejected come from the writer's own library check; checker-found from the two independent checkers. A fixed test set: do not edit.

pairs.label: same
pairs.stem: What is the molecular geometry of xenon [ZEE-non] tetrafluoride?
pairs.note: Same question: 'According to the VSEPR model, what is the molecular geometry of xenon [ZEE-non] tetrafluoride?' (SQUARE PLANAR), down to the pronunciation guide.

pairs.label: same
pairs.stem: Which of the following is a felsic [FEL-sik] intrusive igneous rock?
pairs.note: Same cue and answer: 'Which of the following rock types would be felsic?' with basalt, granite and gabbro among the choices (GRANITE).

pairs.label: same
pairs.stem: What is the term for the channels that pass through plant cell walls and connect the cytoplasm of neighboring cells?
pairs.note: Same cue: 'Name the two types of cell junctions that connect the cytoplasm of adjacent cells' (PLASMODESMATA AND GAP JUNCTION).

pairs.label: same
pairs.stem: Scientists at Argonne National Laboratory are developing cathodes for lithium-ion batteries. In the common cathode material abbreviated NMC, the letters stand for nickel, manganese, and what other metal?
pairs.note: Same lab, topic and answer: 'Scientists at Argonne National Lab are developing lithium-ion battery cathodes that contain manganese instead of what element found in vitamin B12?' (COBALT).

pairs.label: same
pairs.stem: How many positive integer divisors does 360 have?
pairs.note: Same question with the same number: 'The number 360 has how many positive integer factors?' (24).

pairs.label: same
pairs.stem: An object is placed 10 centimeters from a converging lens with a focal length of 20 centimeters. Which of the following best describes the image?
pairs.note: Same question with the same numbers: 'An object is placed 10 centimeters from a double convex lens with a focal length of 20 centimeters. Which of the following types of image will be produced?'

pairs.label: same
pairs.stem: Which of the following planets has the shortest sidereal rotation period?
pairs.note: Same question: 'What planet in our solar system has the shortest rotational period?' (JUPITER).

pairs.label: same
pairs.stem: Two fair six-sided dice are rolled. What is the probability that the sum of the numbers rolled is prime?
pairs.note: Same question: 'Two six-sided dice are rolled. What is the probability that the sum of the two numbers is prime?' (5/12).

pairs.label: same
pairs.stem: A satellite is in a circular orbit around Earth. If the radius of its orbit were quadrupled, by what factor would its orbital period increase?
pairs.note: Same law with the same numbers: a semi-major axis of 4 AU gives a period of 8 years; the draft quadrupled the radius for a factor of 8.

pairs.label: same
pairs.stem: During protein synthesis, what type of RNA molecule carries amino acids to the ribosome?
pairs.note: Same question: 'What type of RNA carries amino acids to the ribosomes?' (tRNA); also doe-ms-03-r05-b12.

pairs.label: same
pairs.stem: Which of the following elements is a metalloid?
pairs.note: Same stem and nearly the same choices: 'Which of the following elements is a metalloid?' (Silicon / Calcium / Iron / Argon); also doe-hs-02-r05-t08.

pairs.label: same
pairs.stem: Which of the following layers of Earth is liquid?
pairs.note: Same cue and answer: 'The lack of transmission of earthquake S-waves through what layer of the Earth is evidence that it is liquid?' (OUTER CORE), with three of the same choices.

pairs.label: same
pairs.stem: What is 15 percent of 80?
pairs.note: Same numbers, inverted: 'What percent of 80 is 12?' (15).

pairs.label: same
pairs.stem: Which of the following is the SI unit of force?
pairs.note: Same question in substance: 'Which of the following SI units can be used to measure weight?' (NEWTON), with joule, watt and newton among the choices; also doe-ms-09-r02-t07 ('the SI unit of mass').

pairs.label: same
pairs.stem: Which of the following is the third most abundant gas in dry air near Earth’s surface?
pairs.note: Same question: 'What gas is the third most abundant gas in the Earth's atmosphere?' (ARGON); also doe-hs-17-r03-t14.

pairs.label: same
pairs.stem: What is the name of the supercontinent that included nearly all of Earth’s land about 250 million years ago?
pairs.note: Same question: 'What is the name given to the supercontinent believed to have existed around 250 million years ago...?' (PANGAEA).

pairs.label: same
pairs.stem: What is the term for the bending of light as it passes at an angle from one material into another, such as from air into water?
pairs.note: Same question: 'What is the term for the bending of a wave as it moves from one medium to another?' (REFRACTION); also doe-hs-10-r08-t06.

pairs.label: same

pairs.stem: Which of the following types of faults forms when tension pulls rocks apart, so that the hanging wall moves down relative to the footwall?
pairs.note: Same cue and answer: 'A fault in the Earth's surface in which the hanging wall has moved down relative to the footwall is called:' (NORMAL FAULT).

pairs.stem: Scientists at the National Energy Technology Laboratory study ways to capture carbon dioxide from power plants. Which of the following energy sources is a fossil fuel?
pairs.note: Same stem: 'Which of the following energy sources is considered a fossil fuel?' (CRUDE OIL).

pairs.label: same
pairs.stem: What is the term for a redox reaction in which atoms of one element, all starting in the same oxidation state, are both oxidized and reduced, as when hydrogen peroxide decomposes into water and oxygen?
pairs.note: Replacement matched: 'What type of redox reaction involves the simultaneous oxidation and reduction of a singular species?' (DISPROPORTIONATION).

pairs.note: Replacement matched almost word for word: 'The webbed hand of a human embryo develops into five separate fingers by a process of programmed cell death. What is the term for this process?' (APOPTOSIS).

pairs.label: same

pairs.label: same

pairs.note: Same numbers: 'Starting from rest, a bike accelerates at 5 meters per second squared for 3 seconds. In meters, what distance did it travel?' (22.5); the draft only added F = ma on top.

pairs.label: same
pairs.stem: A book rests on a table. According to Newton’s third law, which of the following is the reaction force to Earth’s gravitational pull on the book?

pairs.note: First-round replacement matched: 'An object of mass m sits on a flat table. The Earth pulls on the object with force mg. Which of the following is the corresponding reaction force?' (THE OBJECT PULLING UPWARD ON THE EARTH).

pairs.label: same
pairs.stem: In pea plants, the allele for purple flowers is dominant over the allele for white flowers. If two plants that are heterozygous for flower color are crossed, what fraction of their offspring are expected to have white flowers?
pairs.note: Same cue and computation: a cross of two heterozygotes for flower color with red (or purple) dominant over white (3 TO 1); also doe-ms-07-r05-b11.

pairs.label: same

pairs.label: same
pairs.stem: A winter coat stuffed with down feathers keeps a person warm mainly because of which of the following?
pairs.answer: AIR TRAPPED BETWEEN THE FEATHERS CONDUCTS HEAT POORLY
pairs.note: Both ask why down feathers insulate: trapped air.

choices.X: The feathers reflect cold back outside
choices.Y: Air trapped between the feathers conducts heat poorly
